skill.name: python-appservice-deploy
skill.description: Deploy Python Flask, Django, or FastAPI projects to Azure App Service on Linux. The skill guides Azure context selection, resource creation, startup configuration, zip deployment, and post-deploy messaging.
skill.summary: Deploy Python web apps to Azure App Service with Azure CLI or azd guidance.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Azure CLI documentation, PowerShell examples, placeholder URLs, and required App Service bind addresses. The review confirms a high-risk command-injection concern in the retry helper scripts because they execute composed command strings that may include user-supplied Azure resource values.

remediation.issue: Retry helpers execute composed shell command strings.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval and powershell -Command with argument-array execution, or validate resource names against strict Azure-safe patterns before command construction.

remediation.issue: Documentation allows user-specified resource names to be used verbatim.
remediation.suggestion: Document strict validation and shell quoting requirements for app names, resource groups, plans, regions, and subscription values.

remediation.issue: Deployment examples contain many executable command snippets.
remediation.suggestion: Keep commands scoped to Azure CLI and avoid adding network probes, secret reads, or commands unrelated to the requested deployment.

content.user_title: Deploy Python Apps to Azure App Service
content.value_statement: Python web app deployment to Azure App Service requires correct resources, runtime settings, and startup commands. This skill gives a focused workflow for Flask, Django, and FastAPI deployments using Azure CLI or azd.
actual_capabilities: Derives Azure resource group, App Service plan, region, and app names from user context.
Creates or reuses an Azure resource group, Linux App Service plan, and Python web app.
Detects Flask, Django, FastAPI, generic WSGI, generic ASGI, or unknown Python projects.
Sets a FastAPI uvicorn startup command and leaves Flask or Django to Oryx auto-detection.
Deploys code through az webapp deploy or azd deploy when azure.yaml targets App Service.
Prints post-deploy guidance without probing the new endpoint too early.
limitations: It targets Azure App Service Linux for Python web apps only.
It does not build full infrastructure plans, databases, private networking, or IaC templates.
It assumes Azure CLI or azd authentication is already available to the agent environment.
Unknown frameworks may still require the user to provide a custom startup command.

use_cases.title: Ship a Flask prototype
use_cases.description: Deploy a small Flask app to Azure App Service with a generated app name and default Linux plan.

use_cases.title: Move a Django app to App Service
use_cases.description: Create or reuse Azure resources and deploy a Django project while relying on Oryx startup detection.

use_cases.title: Deploy a FastAPI service reliably
use_cases.description: Set the uvicorn startup command and deploy a FastAPI project with server-side build enabled.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy current app
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this Python web app to Azure App Service. Use sensible defaults and ask me only for the app name if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy to existing resources
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a known resource group, region, and app name.
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this FastAPI app to Azure App Service in resource group <resource-group>, region <region>, with app name <app-name>.

prompt_templates.title: Use azd when available
prompt_templates.scenario: Project contains azure.yaml for App Service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this repo has an azure.yaml that targets App Service. If it does, deploy with azd; otherwise use Azure CLI.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose deployment settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this Python project, identify the framework and startup command needs, then deploy to Azure App Service without running endpoint probes after deployment.

output_examples.input: Deploy my Flask project to Azure App Service with defaults.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the derived app name, resource group, plan, region, and Python runtime. It creates missing Azure resources, deploys the zip package, and returns the App Service URL with warm-up guidance.

output_examples.input: Deploy this FastAPI app to an existing resource group.
output_examples.output: The skill detects FastAPI, sets a uvicorn startup command, enables server-side build, deploys the package, and gives the user log commands for optional follow-up.

output_examples.input: This repo has azure.yaml. Deploy it if it targets App Service.
output_examples.output: The skill checks the azure.yaml host target. It uses azd deploy for App Service projects and redirects other hosting targets to broader Azure preparation.

best_practices: Authenticate with Azure CLI or azd before using the skill.
Keep requirements.txt or pyproject.toml current so Oryx can install dependencies during deployment.
Review derived resource names and region before allowing resource creation.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for Azure Functions, Container Apps, AKS, or non-Python workloads.
Do not run early HTTP probes as proof of deployment failure immediately after upload.
Do not pass untrusted shell metacharacters in resource names or command arguments.

faq.question: Which Python frameworks does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Flask, Django, and FastAPI directly. It can deploy other Python web apps, but they may need manual startup settings.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create a resource group, Linux App Service plan, and web app when they are missing.

faq.question: Can it use azd instead of Azure CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses azd when azure.yaml exists and targets App Service.

faq.question: Does it verify the endpoint after deployment?
faq.answer: No. The skill avoids immediate probes because App Service can need several minutes to warm up.

faq.question: Does it manage databases or private networking?
faq.answer: No. Those needs should be handled by a broader Azure infrastructure planning skill.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: The environment needs Azure CLI or azd access for the target subscription. The skill does not provide credentials.
